raw_response:
I have been farming here in Quzhou for 15 years, and with 8 people in my house — some of them working outside to bring back wages — I know I must balance grain for our own stomachs against cash crops. My 19.1 mu is not a large farm, so I put 15 mu into the wheat-maize rotation that I know best, and keep 4.1 mu for cotton to bring in money.

The wheat went into the ground last October before the cold came. Now that spring is here and it is greening up, I will top-dress it with nitrogen fertilizer — urea from the shop — and irrigate it three times from my well: once now at green-up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I buy improved wheat seed every few years because the old seed gives poor germination and lower yield. I will spray twice for weeds and aphids. If the weather does not turn bad, I expect about 520 kg per mu.

Right after we harvest the wheat in early June, there is no time to waste before the rains come, so I plant hybrid maize using no-tillage — I just open a narrow strip and put the seed in. Hybrid maize grows fast and strong, and gives me about 620 kg per mu. I will spread fertilizer at planting and top-dress once later, and irrigate twice — maybe three times if July is too dry. Two sprays for insects and weeds is usually enough.

The cotton on the 4.1 mu is harder work and needs more hands, but my mother-in-law and daughter help with picking. I will rotary till that field in April, plant hybrid cotton seed, and irrigate three times through the summer. Cotton bollworms are a problem here, so I spray four times. I expect about 110 kg of seed cotton per mu.

For all my crops, I put more nitrogen than anything else because that is what pushes the growth. I add phosphorus and potassium too — our soil has been cropped for generations and needs replacing. Having the well means I do not fear dry spells, but pumping costs electricity, so I water only when the plants truly need it.
